name: George III of Great Britain
role: King of Great Britain and Ireland (1760–1820)
summary: George III was a devout Anglican monarch who defended the Crown's prerogatives, notably in choosing ministers. He insisted on suppressing the American rebellion and refused Catholic emancipation in 1801, citing his coronation oath. Much of his reign's policy was made by ministers, so few positions are recorded as his own.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-14): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia's account of peerage creations in 1783-84; the primary page read (s4) records his refusal to create peerages for the Fox-North ministry, which is about patronage, not a position on abolishing hereditary rank.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Issued the 1775 Proclamation for Suppressing Rebellion and Sedition declaring the colonies in open rebellion and ordering officers to suppress it by force.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on who chooses ministers, and the statement now asks only about command of the armed forces.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Reigned as hereditary monarch for sixty years and personally defended Crown prerogatives, including choosing ministers (1783) and refusing Catholic emancipation (1801) as bound by his coronation oath.

national-church-status.rationale: In his letter to Pitt of 1 Feb 1801 he held that his coronation oath bound him to maintain the Church of England as the established church, and refused Catholic emancipation on that ground.

national-self-determination.rationale: Issued the 1775 Proclamation declaring the American colonies, which saw themselves as a people entitled to self-government, in open rebellion to be suppressed, and fought to keep them until 1782-83.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Said he would not be put in the hands of a faction, yet intervened actively in party contests (India Bill 1783, 1807 dismissal); evidence points both ways.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mixed record: he accepted Parliament's role but dismissed a ministry with a Commons majority and tried to sway peers in 1783, resisting a parliamentary check on his choice of ministers.

right-to-secede.rationale: Issued the 1775 Proclamation for Suppressing Rebellion and Sedition, treating the colonies' break from the Crown as rebellion to be suppressed.

notes: Later pass 2026-11-14 (claude-sonnet-5-5): read his letters to Lord North (1768-73 volume, archive.org) and Fortescue's volume for 1782-83 by theme (government, society, world, liberty, economy, means). They deal with patronage, ministries and the American war, so few further statements are settled by his own words or acts. Not obtained: his constitutional essays and the full 1775 speech from the throne.
